title: Newton's Laws of Motion (Foundations of Dynamics)
notes: Newton's first law says a body stays at rest, or keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless a net external force acts on it. A frame in which this is true is an inertial frame.

The second law gives the size and direction of the effect. The net force equals the rate of change of momentum. When the mass is constant this is F_net = ma, and the acceleration points the same way as the net force.

The third law says forces come in pairs. If body A pushes body B, body B pushes body A with the same magnitude and the opposite direction. The two forces act on different bodies, so they do not cancel on one free-body diagram.
Mass measures inertia. For the same net force, a larger mass has a smaller acceleration. Weight is the gravitational force W = mg and is not the same quantity as mass.

A free-body diagram shows only the forces acting on the body you chose. Contact forces such as the normal force and friction are drawn at the surface. The weight is drawn at the centre of gravity, downward.
The normal force from a table and the weight of a book are not a third-law pair. The third-law partner of the book's weight is the gravitational pull of the book on the Earth.

exercises.question: A 2.0 kg block on a smooth horizontal table is pulled horizontally by 10 N. Find the acceleration.
steps: The table is smooth, so the friction force is zero.
Vertically, the normal force balances the weight, so the vertical acceleration is zero.
The horizontal net force is 10 N.
The acceleration is horizontal, in the direction of the pull.
exercises.answer: 5.0 m/s^2 in the direction of the 10 N pull.
